Description: Customer checkout Lambda, its five HTTP API routes and a least-privilege role. Four POST routes require a customer session; GET /ecommerce/service-prices is the one anonymous arm - see ServicePricesRoute's WECARE::WhyAnonymous. Payment initiation is OFF: CHECKOUT_INITIATION_ENABLED is absent on purpose, and both readiness inputs are empty so payment_readiness blocks independently of the flag.

WECARE::ReadThisFirst: This template is the DECLARATION OF RECORD, not the deploy path. The live resources were
created by scripts/provision_checkout.py on 2026-10-01 and are read back by its --verify
mode. It sits beside amplify/infra/home-fallback.json, which has the same relationship to
scripts/home_fallback_dns.py: a reproducible statement of intent for resources that a
It is deliberately NOT wired into amplify/backend.ts. Two reasons, both load-bearing:
1. HTTP API zllr9lrg7j is not CloudFormation-managed. It carries 361 routes created by
provisioning scripts over time, and amplify/link-resources.ts records that the one
HttpApi construct it declares has never been deployed. A CDK construct added here
would create a SECOND API rather than extend this one.
2. amplify/backend.ts states that the Python Lambdas are deployed separately and are not
managed by Amplify Gen 2. Adopting one function into the Amplify stack would put a
live payment-path function under a stack that can delete it on a failed update.
So the routes and integration below reference the existing API by id. Applying this template
to an account that already has these resources will fail on the function name, which is the
correct outcome: the script is the single creator.
WECARE::GateIsOff: Nothing in this template can make a payment possible. CHECKOUT_INITIATION_ENABLED is
absent, EXPECTED_CONFIGURATION_NAME and EXPECTED_PROVIDER_MID are empty strings, and the
role grants no Razorpay credential read. Turning initiation on is an owner-only action and
additionally requires both readiness values from a live Meta/Razorpay readback.

CodeS3Bucket.Description: Bucket holding the deployment ZIP. The provisioner uploads the ZIP inline (Code.ZipFile) instead, so this parameter exists only to make the template self-contained if it is ever applied.

CodeS3Key.Description: Key of the deployment ZIP built by scripts/deploy_all_lambdas.build_zip from amplify/functions/ecommerce/checkout plus the shared lambda_utils tree.

ApiId.Description: The account's single HTTP API (wecare-digital-api). Its only stage is `prod`, which auto-deploys, so a new route is served without an explicit deployment.

Properties.Description: Customer checkout: authoritative Wix total, readiness gate, PaymentAttempt, in-chat handoff. Initiation off by default.

Metadata.WECARE::WhyQualified: The Qualifier is the whole point. A function-level statement does NOT authorise an alias invoke, and the failure is silent: API Gateway answers 500 with no Lambda log line, because the function is never entered. scripts/provision_missing_ui_routes.py records the same trap costing POST /plivo/dial-events.

The original SourceArn was ${ApiId}/*/* : any stage, any method, any path on this API.
Scoped to one API, so never a wildcard over the account, but 360 routes wider than the
two that exist. The obvious replacement was the prefix prod/POST/ecommerce/* . It was
applied, and then measured: another session had added POST /ecommerce/customer-session,
so that prefix already matched a third route belonging to a DIFFERENT function. A prefix
describes a namespace somebody else can grow into, which is not the same as the routes
So there is one statement per route key, each carrying that route's exact source ARN -
no wildcard at all. API Gateway presents {apiId}/{stage}/{METHOD}/{path}. `prod` is
spelled out rather than `*` because it is the only stage on zllr9lrg7j and there is no
apigateway-invoke-checkout-ecommerce) were removed only AFTER the per-route statements
were added: add_permission cannot edit a statement, and remove-then-add under one id
leaves a window where the routes resolve to a target API Gateway cannot invoke.

Metadata.WECARE::WhySeparate: One statement per route. See CheckoutInvokePermission's WECARE::WhyOneStatementPerRoute - a shared /ecommerce/* prefix already matched another function's route.

Metadata.WECARE::Consumer: src/pages/cart.tsx POSTs ${API_BASE}/ecommerce/checkout with a Bearer token.

src/pages/checkout/status.tsx POSTs ${API_BASE}/ecommerce/checkout/status. handler._action resolves `status` off the path suffix, so both route keys land on the right branch. Deliberately two explicit routes rather than a {proxy+}: the surface stays exactly as wide as its two consumers.

src/pages/cart.tsx POSTs ${API_BASE}/ecommerce/prepare-checkout with a Bearer token and {action, lineItems, requestKey}. handler._action resolves `prepare` off the path suffix. The route exists in scripts/provision_checkout.ROUTE_KEYS and was missing here, which is what test_the_template_matches_the_route_arns_the_script_grants measured.

src/pages/cart.tsx POSTs ${API_BASE}/ecommerce/verify-callback with the browser's razorpay_payment_id / razorpay_order_id / razorpay_signature. The HMAC is verified against the SERVER-STORED gateway order id, never the relayed one, and a valid signature is still only a trigger: an authenticated capture readback is required before any paid state.

Metadata.WECARE::WhySeparate: One statement per route, with an EXACT SourceArn and no wildcard. See CheckoutInvokePermission's WECARE::WhyOneStatementPerRoute: a shared prod/POST/ecommerce/* prefix already matched another function's route.

Metadata.WECARE::Consumer: src/lib/servicePricing.ts GETs ${API_BASE}/ecommerce/service-prices from the four public service pages (/submit-request/, /request-amendment/, /drop-docs/, /vault/) so each card shows its own variant's LIVE Wix price. Owner decision 2026-10-08: a price must be changeable in Wix with no deploy.
WECARE::WhyAnonymous: This is the ONE route on this function that is not behind require_customer, and the
exemption is deliberate rather than an oversight.
A visitor reads the price BEFORE signing in - the price is what decides whether they
sign in at all - so there is no customer identity available to authenticate. The arm is
narrow by construction: GET only, one exact path, and handler._service_prices accepts no
path parameter, no query string and no body, so nothing a caller supplies reaches Wix or
a table. It returns only Wix-live prices in integer paise and cannot mutate anything.
POST on the same path still requires a session: handler.handler gates the pre-auth arm
on the method as well as the path, and the SourceArn below pins GET, so the exemption
cannot widen to POST at the permission layer either.
The exemption is recorded in TWO files by design - scripts/audit_route_auth.py
EXPECTED_PUBLIC_ROUTES and tests/test_route_auth_enforcement.py's literal set - so
exempting a route takes two edits rather than one.
WECARE::Throttle: 5 rps sustained / 10 burst, as a RouteSettings entry on the prod stage. Applied by
scripts/provision_checkout.py (ensure_route_throttle) and read back by its --verify,
NOT declared here: the prod stage is shared by ~361 routes on an API this template
only takes as a parameter, so declaring AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Stage would claim ownership
of configuration belonging to every other function.
WHY IT EXISTS. A cache MISS on this route costs eight Wix calls (get + estimate per
variant) on the same API key the live checkout prices real baskets with, so anonymous
traffic here can induce provider throttling that reaches the payment path. The /api/*
edge was measured caching a public max-age response on 2026-10-08, which keeps origin
volume to roughly one fill per PoP per minute - but that is someone else's
configuration and could change silently. This cap does not depend on it.
Exceeding it is a 429, which src/lib/servicePricing.ts already renders as
'temporarily unavailable' with no pay CTA. It fails closed, never at a guessed price.

Metadata.WECARE::WhySeparate: One statement per route, with an EXACT SourceArn and no wildcard. The METHOD in the ARN is load-bearing here: it is what keeps the anonymous exemption to GET.
Metadata.WECARE::NoNewIam: The arm needs nothing the role does not already hold - it reads the Wix key (ReadWixApiKey) and the commerce-keys table (PaymentAttemptAndCommerceKeys) that the checkout path already uses, so no policy statement changes.
